current branch name matches the generated pattern (`echo "$BRANCH" | grep -E "^(feat|fix|docs|chore|refactor)/[a-z0-9-]+$"`).

A high-stakes gate verdict or audit (Phase 1/3/4/8, code-review, security-review) is produced **via the `midas-orchestrator` sub-agent** — its pinned `model:` is the provenance. The model id written into an audit/verify/tribunal record header is **provenance-by-delegation, not self-report**; a record produced on the inherited session model must not claim a tier it did not run on.

*(manual)* Under any `execution_mode`, a binding gate/audit/verify verdict header (Phase 1/3/4/8, code-review, security-review) names a **Claude `orchestrate`** model as provenance; a local model id in a binding verdict header is a fail — it may appear only on a record explicitly marked `un-attested`.

Doc fetches and file/status extraction are delegated to `midas-scout` (or `Explore`), not run on the orchestrate tier. *(manual: a phase whose only work is fetch/extract names a scout delegation in its SKILL body.)*
Each multi-tier phase delegates its produce/fetch legs to `midas-builder` / `midas-scout` in the SKILL body — `harness-tier` is the dispatch tier only, never the whole cost story. *(manual.)*

`paths.state -> routing` ids equal `resolveCostAwareRouting(routing_profile, cost_profile)` under the Claude profile (any `cost_profile`); agent pins match the same map. Run `node <paths.scripts>/doctor.mjs <project>`; a `routing:*` warning is a fail.

`manual:` each test targets one behaviour; a test asserting several unrelated outcomes is a fail.
`manual:` test titles name scenario + expected result; a title that is just the function name is a fail.
`grep -rnE "\.(skip|only)|xit\(|xfail|@pytest.mark.skip|test.todo" <tests>` → each match carries a linked issue + expiry, else fail.
`grep -rnE "assert\s+True|expect\((true|1)\)\.toBe\(\1\)|assert 1 == 1" <tests>` → empty.
the suite passes when run in random/sharded order; shared mutable state across tests is a fail.
`grep -rnE "https?://(?!localhost|127\.0\.0\.1)" <tests>` → empty, or each match is a tagged contract test.
`manual:` filesystem-touching tests use a tmp dir and clean up in teardown.
`grep -rnE "Math.random|Date.now\(\)|new Date\(\)" <tests>` reviewed; unseeded randomness or a real clock in a time-dependent test is a fail.
the CI workflow (`.github/workflows/*`) runs the test command on push/PR; absent, it is a fail.
`manual:` branch protection / required check makes the test job mandatory for merge.
`manual:` any known-flaky test has a tracking issue and a fix/quarantine within the sprint.
the project's typecheck, lint, and build commands (`tsc --noEmit` / `mypy`, the linter, the build) each exit 0 with zero new errors on the sprint diff.

checks.body: `manual:` on each key screen, exactly one primary CTA is visually dominant; a second filled primary on the same view is a fail.
`grep -rniE "<h[1-6]" <ui-src>` → `manual:` each page's heading order has no skipped levels; a decorative size bump without semantic level is a fail.

`manual:` the primary heading uses `--ds-text-2xl`/`--ds-text-3xl` or larger; body copy uses `--ds-text-md`; metadata/labels use `--ds-text-sm` or `--ds-text-secondary` — a screen where all text reads the same size/weight is a fail.
`grep -rniE "font-family" <ui-src>` → every declaration is `var(--ds-font-sans)` or `var(--ds-font-mono)` (or inherits from the base reset); a third family or a raw stack name is a fail.
`grep -rniE "font-size:[[:space:]]*[0-9.]+(px|rem|em)" <ui-src>` → each hit is `var(--ds-text-*)` or lives in the token definition file; a raw size in component code is a fail.
`grep -rniE "line-height:[[:space:]]*[0-9.]+" <ui-src>` → each hit in component code is `var(--ds-leading-*)`; a raw unitless/px line-height in a component is a fail.

`manual:` related controls share `--ds-space-2`/`--ds-space-4` gaps; unrelated sections are separated by ≥ `--ds-space-6`; arbitrary px gaps in component CSS are a fail (see `components.md` cross-cutting rule 6).

`manual:` the primary CTA uses `--ds-action-*`; status badges/toasts use intent tokens; a decorative rainbow of accent colours on one screen is a fail. Hardcoded colour values are graded under `accessibility.md` (do not re-audit here).
`manual:` primary vs secondary/ghost variants are distinguishable without relying on colour alone (weight, fill vs outline, or position).
`manual:` name the first-viewport composition; if it matches the default SaaS stack above with no written justification in design-direction, fail (severity MED+).
